Explores core experimental techniques used in biomedical and pharmaceutical research.
Supports students before or during independent research, and emphasizes practical skill development, quantitative reasoning, and the connection between experimental data and biological or pharmacological questions.
Students will learn how to design assays, generate and analyze data, and evaluate experimental results with an emphasis on accuracy, reproducibility, and good laboratory practice.
Students will select specialized experimental modules aligned with their research interests or future laboratory placements.

Research topics may span areas such as drug discovery, pharmacology, toxicology, pharmaceutics, pharmacokinetics, environmental health, and natural products.
Through structured presentations and discussion, students develop skills in scientific communication, data interpretation, and critical evaluation of research.
Exposes participants to diverse research approaches within pharmaceutical sciences, helping students connect laboratory research with concepts

learned in the classroom.
Students will strengthen their ability to present scientific work professionally, ask thoughtful questions, and engage in scholarly discussion—skills essential for graduate study, professional programs, and careers in biomedical research. 2019-1 Page 1 of 4 Revised 04/02/2020 RFQ – AGENCY SOLICITATION SPECIFICATIONS TITLE: RFQ24004253 URI HVAC Maintenance And Repair Contract SECTION B: SCOPE OF WORK AND REQUIREMENTS University of Rhode Island (URI) is seeking a vendor for HVAC Maintenance and Repair.
Scope of Work : URI has approximately 300 buildings on several sites The buildings range in age from new 2020 to 125 years old with all of types of HVAC systems.
The vendor shall supply services, parts, tools and material for a variety of heating ventilating and air conditioning (HVAC) equipment, of various manufacture, located throughout the University's main Kingston campus as well as the university of Rhode Island's W.
Alton Jones West Greenwich campus, the University's Narragansett Bay campus and the University's Feinstein campus located in Providence as well as all other URI facilities.

Services are to include but not limited to repair maintenance of gas and oil fired heaters, hot water systems, repairs to VRF systems, duct work repair and maintenance of various sizes, rooftop units, steam to hot water convertors, pipe and duct insulation, fan coil units, cabinet heaters, split package air-conditioning units, unit ventilators, and assorted thermostatically controlled devices.
Service includes repair, maintenance, calibration and replacement of all components of these devices as required.
The vendor must have the ability to adjust and calibrate the controls associated with these units.
The vendor must have the basic knowledge of the interaction of the listed devices as they relate to the transmission and communication with energy management systems in order to properly diagnose and trouble shoot the devices.
As an example: the vendor must understand pneumatic controls application and calibration, direct digital control application and diagnostics and the interaction between these two systems.
The vendor must have the ability to provide piping repair as it relates to these devices both pneumatically and for water and other liquid and gaseous media transmission.

Any specialty sub-contractor will be paid per the RI prevailing wage rates.
This includes but not limited to, plastic, copper, black iron, pipe insulation and other piping.
